 Prediction 
 In the second round of Australia’s A-League, Brisbane Roar will host reigning champions Auckland at Suncorp Stadium. The hosts opened the season with a win and will look to build on that success, while the visitors will aim to bounce back from a surprise defeat. Despite the gap in the teams’ achievements, this clash promises to be a tightly contested affair.
 Read also: Northern derby amid squad losses: prediction for Lille vs Lens 
 Brisbane Roar: a positive start after a prolonged crisis
 Brisbane opened their campaign with a 2-1 win over Perth Glory. The team put in a confident first-half performance and managed to hold on to their lead, gaining a valuable boost of confidence ahead of their meeting with the champions.
 However, one successful match does not erase the problems of previous years. Roar have finished outside the top six for five consecutive seasons. Head coach Michael Valkanis can also point to few consistent results: under his leadership, the team have won just seven of 27 matches.
 Their attacking struggles are particularly evident. Last season, Brisbane scored just 27 goals in 26 matches — the worst record in the league. To stand a chance of picking up points against Auckland, the hosts will need to be far more clinical with their opportunities.
 Auckland: it is time for the champions to regain their confidence
 Auckland head into the away fixture after a painful 2-5 defeat to Western Sydney Wanderers. Conceding five goals against a team that finished last in the previous season is a worrying signal for the reigning champions.
 New head coach Pedro Moreira is still putting his playing system in place. In the team’s first three matches under his management, Auckland have recorded one win and suffered two defeats. The Portuguese coach’s main task is to restore the defence’s former solidity.
 Last season, Auckland had the second-best defence in the league, conceding 29 goals in 26 matches. If the visitors can regain their discipline and cut down on mistakes, their attacking potential should be enough to secure a positive result.
 Match facts and head-to-head record
 Brisbane Roar have never beaten Auckland in their previous four competitive meetings
 Auckland have won three of their four head-to-head matches, with the other ending in a draw
 Last season, Brisbane scored 27 goals in 26 matches, while Auckland conceded 29 goals over the same period
 Champions’ defence under scrutiny: prediction for Brisbane Roar vs Auckland
 Brisbane gained the confidence they needed after a strong start and will look to make the most of home advantage. However, the head-to-head record is firmly against them: Auckland have consistently found ways to neutralise the hosts’ attack.
 The visitors have enough quality to respond to their recent defeat, but conceding five goals in the previous round raises doubts about the reliability of their defence. Given both teams’ attacking capabilities and their inconsistent starts to the season, the most likely outcome appears to be a match in which both sides score.

 Both teams to score - Yes
